title: 12 Days: Nero's succession and the fall of the Byzantine Empire

sentences.en: Hello, welcome to The Rest is History and Happy New Year.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎收听《历史的余韵》，新年快乐。

sentences.en: We have finally reached 2022 and we've finally reached the 1st of January in our 12 or 13 days of Christmas.
sentences.zh: 我们终于迎来了2022年，也终于迎来了圣诞节十二或十三天假期的第一天，也就是1月1日。

sentences.en: So Tom, Tom Holland, to bring in the new year, what jolly, upbeat, laugh-a-minute story have you chosen for us?
sentences.zh: 那么汤姆，汤姆·霍兰德，为了迎接新年，你为我们准备了什么有趣、欢快、让人捧腹的故事吗？

sentences.en: Well, it's a Roman story and I think that's appropriate because we celebrate the 1st of January as the new year because of the Romans.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个罗马故事，我觉得很应景，因为我们庆祝1月1日作为新年，正是源于罗马人。

sentences.en: Was it the first day of the year for them?
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，那是每年的第一天吗？

sentences.en: Was that March, I thought?
sentences.zh: 我记得应该是三月吧？

sentences.en: Yes, it was, but it was the first day of the civil year.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实是三月，但1月1日是民事年度的第一天。

sentences.en: So it's when the consuls, who are the two magistrates who during the Republican period served as the kind of preeminent magistrates in the Republic, it's when they took office.
sentences.zh: 所以，这一天是执政官——也就是共和国时期担任共和国最高行政长官的那两位官员——正式就职的日子。

sentences.en: And from the 2nd century BC onwards and increasingly under the Caesars, it comes to be enshrined as the start of the year more generally as well.
sentences.zh: 从公元前2世纪开始，在凯撒统治下，这一天也逐渐被确立为更广泛意义上的新年伊始。

sentences.en: So I think we talked about that, didn't we?
sentences.zh: 我想我们之前讨论过这个，对吧？

sentences.en: We talked on an episode about New Year and about Janus, the two-headed god who looked both ways.
sentences.zh: 我们在某一期节目里聊过新年和雅努斯，就是那个长着两张脸、能同时看向两边的神。

sentences.en: And so under the empire, under the Caesars, the 1st of January is not only the day in which the consuls head up, up onto the capital,
sentences.zh: 在帝国时期，在凯撒们的统治下，1月1日不仅是执政官登上卡比托利欧山的日子，

sentences.en: which is the sacred hill with the great shrine of Jupiter and sacrifices made there and the auguries are taken and people look to the future.
sentences.zh: 那里是神圣的山丘，有朱庇特的神庙，人们在那里举行祭祀、占卜，并展望未来。

sentences.en: But it's also a day in which offerings are kind of made, sacrifices are made to the good of Caesar.
sentences.zh: 这一天也是人们为凯撒的福祉进行献祭和祭祀的日子。

sentences.en: And in AD 68, that is the year, it's the last year of Nero's life and he goes up there.
sentences.zh: 而在公元68年，也就是尼禄生命的最后一年，他去了那里。

sentences.en: And notoriously what happens on that day is, first of all, they can't find the keys to the temple of the Flying Jove.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，那天发生了一件怪事：首先，他们找不到飞天朱庇特神庙的钥匙。

sentences.en: So that's literally ominous.
sentences.zh: 这简直是不祥之兆。

sentences.en: That's ominous.
sentences.zh: 确实不祥。

sentences.en: But the other ominous thing that happens is that Sporus, who, a friend of the show, the poor boy who has been castrated and turned into the spitting image of Nero's dead wife,
sentences.zh: 但另一件不祥的事是，斯波鲁斯——我们节目的老朋友，那个可怜的男孩，他被阉割并被整容成尼禄亡妻的模样——

sentences.en: Papaya Sabina, as a gift, gives Nero a ring on which Persephone is shown being raped by Hades, the king of the underworld,
sentences.zh: 也就是波培娅·萨宾娜，他送给尼禄一枚戒指作为新年礼物，上面刻着冥王哈迪斯强暴珀耳塞福涅的场景，

sentences.en: and taken down into the depths of the kingdom of the dead.
sentences.zh: 并将她带入死者王国的深处。

sentences.en: It's quite a strong present, I would say.
sentences.zh: 这礼物可真是够劲儿的。

sentences.en: Well, yes, all kinds of subliminal messages.
sentences.zh: 是啊，充满了各种潜意识的暗示。

sentences.en: Especially what's been going on with Sporus.
sentences.zh: 尤其是考虑到斯波鲁斯的遭遇。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: So it's remembered subsequently as a sombre moment where Nero's downfall, which happens over the course of the following months, is set in train.
sentences.zh: 所以后来人们记得这是一个阴郁的时刻，尼禄的垮台——发生在接下来的几个月里——就是从这一刻开始的。

sentences.en: And it's set in train by a Gallo-Roman aristocrat called Julius Vindex, who declares that Nero's beyond the pale, he's gone too far, he's raising the banner of rebellion.
sentences.zh: 而这一切是由一位名叫尤利乌斯·温代克斯的高卢-罗马贵族引发的，他宣称尼禄已经不可救药，做得太过分了，于是竖起了反叛的大旗。

sentences.en: And this serves to trigger a rebellion in Spain and encourages an old school kind of figure of republican aristocratic virtue called Galba,
sentences.zh: 这引发了西班牙的叛乱，并鼓励了一位具有老派共和贵族美德的人物——加尔巴，

sentences.en: who is the governor of one of the provinces in Spain to declare himself emperor.
sentences.zh: 他当时是西班牙某行省的总督，他宣布自己为皇帝。

sentences.en: Nero is toppled, commits suicide, and the Senate accept Galba as emperor.
sentences.zh: 尼禄被推翻并自杀，元老院接受加尔巴为皇帝。

sentences.en: And Galba crosses from Spain through Gaul down through Italy and enters Rome.
sentences.zh: 加尔巴从西班牙穿过高卢，南下意大利，进入罗马。

sentences.en: And so on the 1st of January 69 AD, he is the emperor.
sentences.zh: 所以到了公元69年1月1日，他就是皇帝了。

sentences.en: So he is going through the rituals that the year before Nero had done.
sentences.zh: 因此，他正在经历尼禄前一年所经历的那些仪式。

sentences.en: Now, these rituals do not just take place in Rome.
sentences.zh: 现在，这些仪式不仅仅是在罗马举行。

sentences.en: They take place in cities across the empire.
sentences.zh: 它们在帝国各地的城市中举行。

sentences.en: And most significantly, they take place in legionary bases.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，它们在军团驻地举行。

sentences.en: And these legionary bases are dotted mainly around the frontiers.
sentences.zh: 这些军团驻地主要分布在边境地区。

sentences.en: Not exclusively, but mainly.
sentences.zh: 虽然不全是，但主要是。

sentences.en: And the largest concentration of these legionary bases are along the Rhine, because the Rhine obviously is adjacent to Germany that the Romans had attempted to conquer.
sentences.zh: 这些军团驻地最集中的地方是在莱茵河沿岸，因为莱茵河显然毗邻罗马人试图征服的日耳曼地区。

sentences.en: They then lost three legions to Varus in AD 9.
sentences.zh: 他们在公元9年输给了瓦鲁斯三个军团。

sentences.en: Varus's three legions had been lost to Arminius in AD 9.
sentences.zh: 瓦鲁斯的那三个军团在公元9年被阿米尼乌斯消灭了。

sentences.en: Tudorberg ForeSt.
sentences.zh: 条顿堡森林。

sentences.en: Tudorberg ForeSt.
sentences.zh: 条顿堡森林。

sentences.en: And the Romans kind of, they inflict devastating punishment on the Germans for it.
sentences.zh: 罗马人对日耳曼人进行了毁灭性的惩罚。

sentences.en: And they essentially decide the Germans don't deserve to be conquered.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上认为日耳曼人不值得征服。

sentences.en: That's their attitude.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们的态度。

sentences.en: So they build these line of bases along the Rhine.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在莱茵河沿岸建立了一道防线。

sentences.en: And that means that there's a huge concentration of manpower there.
sentences.zh: 这意味着那里集中了大量的兵力。

sentences.en: Now, these Rhine legions, they had marched against Julius Vindex in the summer.
sentences.zh: 这些莱茵河军团在夏天曾向尤利乌斯·温代克斯进军。

sentences.en: Not because they were loyal to Nero, but because they saw Julius Vindex, not as a Roman, but as a Gallic rebel.
sentences.zh: 不是因为他们忠于尼禄，而是因为他们把尤利乌斯·温代克斯视为高卢叛军，而非罗马人。

sentences.en: And there'd been attempts to negotiate, but basically between the commander of the Rhine legions and Julius Vindex.
sentences.zh: 莱茵河军团的指挥官和尤利乌斯·温代克斯之间曾有过谈判的尝试。

sentences.en: But the legions wanted to have a punch up.
sentences.zh: 但军团士兵们想打一仗。

sentences.en: They want, basically, they wanted, you know, they wanted a chance to wipe out Julius Vindex's men who were all Gauls.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上是想找个机会消灭尤利乌斯·温代克斯的手下，那些人全是高卢人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that would then license them to plunder Gaul.
sentences.zh: 那样他们就能获得劫掠高卢的许可。

sentences.en: I was about to say, there must be some reason other than just fighting.
sentences.zh: 我正想说，除了打仗之外肯定还有其他原因。

sentences.en: They would have a big punch up and they want booty.
sentences.zh: 他们想大干一场，然后抢夺战利品。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And they're not allowed to do this.
sentences.zh: 但他们不被允许这样做。

sentences.en: And basically, it's Galba who stops them from doing it.
sentences.zh: 基本上是加尔巴阻止了他们。

sentences.en: And Galba sends them packing back to the Rhine bases.
sentences.zh: 加尔巴把他们打发回了莱茵河的驻地。

sentences.en: So they're really, really cross about this.
sentences.zh: 所以他们对此非常、非常愤怒。

sentences.en: And they're further, they dislike Galba because Galba had been in command on the Rhine frontier.
sentences.zh: 而且他们更不喜欢加尔巴，因为加尔巴曾经在莱茵河边境指挥过他们。

sentences.en: And he was a tremendous kind of martinet.
sentences.zh: 他是个极其严厉的教官。

sentences.en: He was, you know, an old school stickler.
sentences.zh: 他是个老派的死板教条主义者。

sentences.en: And they didn't like it.
sentences.zh: 他们不喜欢这样。

sentences.en: And he was, he was kind of, legionaries were perfectly capable of respecting stern disciplinarians, but they had to be charismatic as well.
sentences.zh: 军团士兵完全能够尊重严厉的纪律，但指挥官也必须有个人魅力。

sentences.en: And it's kind of football manager.
sentences.zh: 就像足球教练一样。

sentences.en: You know, Dominic, all that stuff that you were doing when you should have been.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你当时做的事情，本该在那个时候做的。

sentences.en: You're comparing Galba's administration of the Rhine legions to my managerial career and championship manager in the late 1990s.
sentences.zh: 你是在拿加尔巴管理莱茵河军团，和我90年代末在《冠军足球经理》里的执教生涯做比较吗？

sentences.en: There are managers who can be incredible sticklers for discipline and who nobody likes.
sentences.zh: 有些教练对纪律要求极其严格，但没人喜欢他们。

sentences.en: And then there are managers who are incredible sticklers for discipline and the players absolutely adore them and will do anything for them.
sentences.zh: 也有一些教练对纪律要求极其严格，但球员们却非常崇拜他们，愿意为他们做任何事。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Galba was a stickler without charisma.
sentences.zh: 加尔巴就是那种没有魅力的死板教官。

sentences.en: So he's not Alex Ferguson, basically.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上不是亚历克斯·弗格森。

sentences.en: He's not Alex Ferguson, no.
sentences.zh: 他不是亚历克斯·弗格森，确实不是。

sentences.en: So they don't like him.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不喜欢他。

sentences.en: And that means that when the 1st of January comes and the time comes for them to go to the Principia,
sentences.zh: 这意味着当1月1日到来，他们该去军团驻地中央的“统帅部”时，

sentences.en: which is the kind of the central great hall, the great shrine in the middle of each legionary base,
sentences.zh: 也就是每个军团驻地中间那个宏伟的大厅和神龛，

sentences.en: to pay their respects to the standards, the eagles, that is the symbol for each legion, but also the statues of the emperor.
sentences.zh: 去向军旗、鹰徽——那是每个军团的象征——以及皇帝的雕像致敬时，

sentences.en: And it's a way basically of kind of renewing, you know, it's a public affirmation of loyalty.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是一种更新，一种公开的忠诚宣誓。

sentences.en: To the serving emperor.
sentences.zh: 对现任皇帝的忠诚。

sentences.en: And this is incredibly important this year of all years, because Galba, unlike the previous lines of emperors,
sentences.zh: 这在今年显得尤为重要，因为加尔巴与之前的历任皇帝不同，

sentences.en: you know, he has no claim to be a part of the family of Augustus, who was the founder of this imperial dynasty.
sentences.zh: 他没有任何理由声称自己是奥古斯都家族的一员，而奥古斯都正是这个帝国王朝的奠基人。

sentences.en: So for the first time, someone is ruling a Caesar who does not belong to the family of the Caesars.
sentences.zh: 所以这是第一次，统治凯撒帝国的人不属于凯撒家族。

sentences.en: So you have all these, all these bases.
sentences.zh: 所以你有所有这些驻地。

sentences.en: You have bases in what are called lower Germany, which is the kind of the upper Rhine, the Rhine nearest the North Sea.
sentences.zh: 你有下日耳曼行省的驻地，也就是莱茵河上游，靠近北海的那一段。

sentences.en: And then you have upper Germany, which is going further towards the source.
sentences.zh: 然后是上日耳曼行省，那是往源头方向走的。

sentences.en: The legions of lower Germany, with no great enthusiasm, are persuaded to basically kind of swear loyalty, swear their sacramentum, their kind of oath of loyalty to Galba.
sentences.zh: 下日耳曼的军团在毫无热情的情况下，被说服去宣誓效忠，宣誓他们的“忠诚誓言”，也就是对加尔巴的效忠。

sentences.en: In upper Germany, it's different.
sentences.zh: 在上日耳曼，情况则不同。

sentences.en: There, there is a massive troublemaker by the name of Aulus Caecina.
sentences.zh: 那里有一个巨大的麻烦制造者，名叫奥卢斯·凯基纳。

sentences.en: And Caecina actually had been a colleague in Spain of Galba's.
sentences.zh: 凯基纳实际上曾是加尔巴在西班牙的同事。

sentences.en: Oh, so he hates him.
sentences.zh: 哦，所以他恨他。

sentences.en: No, I had actually kind of swung around behind him.
sentences.zh: 不，我其实是想说他已经倒戈了。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧。

sentences.en: Together with a man called Otho, who would be a friend of Nero.
sentences.zh: 他和奥托一起，奥托曾是尼禄的朋友。

sentences.en: So Otho Caecina.
sentences.zh: 所以是奥托和凯基纳。

sentences.en: You love him.
sentences.zh: 你很喜欢他。

sentences.en: You love Otho.
sentences.zh: 你很喜欢奥托。

sentences.en: Otho Caecina and Vitalius.
sentences.zh: 奥托、凯基纳和维特里乌斯。

sentences.en: So Otho Caecina and Galba, between them, had kind of mustered the forces of Spain that had then enabled Galba to become emperor.
sentences.zh: 所以奥托、凯基纳和加尔巴联手，集结了西班牙的军队，这使得加尔巴能够成为皇帝。

sentences.en: Otho had gone with Galba to Rome, but by Caecina, who was very young, had been given command of the senior legion in a double legionary base at a place called Magonti-Arcum,
sentences.zh: 奥托随加尔巴去了罗马，但凯基纳非常年轻，被任命为马贡蒂亚库姆（即今天的美因茨）双军团驻地的资深军团指挥官，

sentences.en: which today is Mainz.
sentences.zh: 也就是今天的马因茨。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And this is a huge promotion.
sentences.zh: 这是一次巨大的提拔。

sentences.en: He's been promoted massively above, you know, his age qualifications.
sentences.zh: 他的职位远远超过了他的年龄资历。

sentences.en: So Caecina should be happy with this, but he's not because he's a man in a hurry.
sentences.zh: 所以凯基纳本该为此感到高兴，但他并不，因为他是个急于求成的人。

sentences.en: And he's stuck out in, you know, in the snow and drizzle of the Rhine, while Otho is back in Rome, whooping it up.
sentences.zh: 他被困在莱茵河的雨雪中，而奥托却在罗马寻欢作乐。

sentences.en: And of course, as it turns out, plotting.
sentences.zh: 当然，事实证明，他还在密谋。

sentences.en: And Caecina basically decides that he wants to expedite his career even faster.
sentences.zh: 凯基纳基本上决定要加快他的晋升速度。

sentences.en: And so over the course of 69, he's been engaging in all kinds of corrupt practices, and he's been caught red-handed, and Galba wants to bring him to trial.
sentences.zh: 所以在69年期间，他一直在进行各种腐败行为，结果被当场抓获，加尔巴想要审判他。

sentences.en: And so this threatens the total ruin of his career.
sentences.zh: 这威胁到了他职业生涯的彻底毁灭。

sentences.en: So Caecina decides on the 1st of January he's got nothing to lose.
sentences.zh: 所以凯基纳决定在1月1日破釜沉舟。

sentences.en: And so he stirs up a mutiny.
sentences.zh: 他煽动了一场兵变。

sentences.en: And the legion he's in command of, and then the other legion that's sharing this camp, they all smash the statues of Galba.
sentences.zh: 他指挥的军团，以及驻扎在同一个营地的另一个军团，都砸碎了加尔巴的雕像。

sentences.en: They reject his claim to be a legitimate Caesar.
sentences.zh: 他们拒绝承认他作为合法凯撒的地位。

sentences.en: They swear an oath of loyalty, not to any individual candidate, because there isn't an available one, but to the Senate and people of Rome.
sentences.zh: 他们宣誓效忠的不是某个具体的候选人，因为当时没有合适的人选，而是效忠于罗马元老院和人民。

sentences.en: But of course, they are immediately looking around for someone else who might be able to, you know, take Galba's place.
sentences.zh: 但当然，他们立刻开始寻找其他人来取代加尔巴。

sentences.en: So even Caecina recognizes that he can't do that.
sentences.zh: 所以即使是凯基纳也意识到他自己做不到。

sentences.en: He's too young.
sentences.zh: 他太年轻了。

sentences.en: He's too junior.
sentences.zh: 资历太浅。

sentences.en: He lacks the prestige to be a credible Caesar.
sentences.zh: 他缺乏成为一名可信凯撒的威望。

sentences.en: So basically, it needs to be either the governor of Upper Germany or Lower Germany.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，人选必须是上日耳曼或下日耳曼的总督。

sentences.en: The governor of Upper Germany has one of the more amusingly, one of the more amusing Roman names.
sentences.zh: 上日耳曼总督的名字非常有趣，是罗马名字里比较好笑的一个。

sentences.en: I mean, he's called Hordonius Flaccus, which, I mean, this kind of sounds like something out of Viz.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他叫霍多尼乌斯·弗拉库斯，这听起来就像是《Viz》杂志里的名字。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he's a hopeless figure.
sentences.zh: 他是个无可救药的人。

sentences.en: He's flaccid.
sentences.zh: 他很“软弱”（Flaccid）。

sentences.en: He is a flaccid figure.
sentences.zh: 他确实是个软弱的人。

sentences.en: He's not a hard-on.
sentences.zh: 他可不是个硬汉。

sentences.en: He basically, he's not going to be a good Caesar.
sentences.zh: 他基本上不可能是个好凯撒。

sentences.en: And so they look at the guy who is, you know, up the Rhine, who's the governor there, and it's a guy called Vitellius.
sentences.zh: 所以他们看向莱茵河上游的那位总督，那个人叫维特里乌斯。

sentences.en: Very fat.
sentences.zh: 非常胖。

sentences.zh: 现在，正如你所说，维特里乌斯非常、非常胖。

sentences.zh: 加尔巴被奥托谋杀，奥托在战斗中被维特里乌斯击败，而维特里乌斯又被韦斯巴芗的支持者击败并惨死，

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，相比之下，你知道，罗马人，那些住在君士坦丁堡的人，过着一种镀金般的辉煌生活，真的，
